correctness.rationale: For odd N=2m+1, conditional negative type is exactly negativity of all circulant powered-distance Fourier multipliers F_{N,k}(p). The discrete second difference identity in RESULT.md isolates the positive (p>1) convexity weights b_r>=0. Odd Fourier modes remain negative, while even modes require H_{N,k}>0. At delta=c/N^2, all even k>=log N are controlled by H>=2k^2/N^2-O(c log N/N^2). Uniform low-mode Taylor/Riemann estimates give N^2 H_{N,k}=pi^2 k^2/2-c J_k+o(1), where J_k=int_0^{pi k}(1-cos u)/u du. For k=2j, the pointwise trigonometric inequality 1-cos(jv)<=j^2(1-cos v) yields J_{2j}<=j^2 J_2. Thus all modes are negative for fixed c<2pi^2/J_2 and the k=2 mode becomes positive when c exceeds it; downward closure gives N^2(beta_N-1)->2pi^2/J_2=8.09762735686653... for N odd. Independent all-mode numerical checks N=101,201,401 corroborate but do not prove asymptotics. No assertion of finite-N mode-two exact dominance.

value.rationale: The supremal negative-type exponent of a standard odd cycle metric is a natural quantitative invariant for Hilbertian snowflake embeddings. Closing the gap between a known single-frequency necessary obstruction and a sufficient all-frequency inequality requires genuine uniform spectral analysis as N grows and yields the sharp previously unknown N^-2 correction.
